chapter: Own groups, bebop and Savoy sessions
title: Cole's quintet and sextet of 1948-49

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: mentions your regular studio work 1946 to '48, led own quintet in 1948 to sextet in early 1949. Let's talk about those.
What is that in '48 and '49.
And with regular studio work '46 to '48. Which implies that when you had your own groups you weren't doing much studio work.

No I wasn't, no I wasn't doing too much studio work then. I had sextet and we'd go out on gigs and things, go to Toronto, Philadelphia, different things, two weeks, three weeks, come back you know and do things, go in the Metropole.
Who was with you?
My brother playing piano.
Teddy?
Jay. Jay. Jay was playing piano, Monkey Johnson.
The trumpet player.
Trumpet player. Barney Bigard, clarinet. Chambers on trombone.
Henderson Chambers?
Yeah Henderson Chambers, Mr. Chambers we used to call him.
Why was that?
Well he was so nice, everybody just respected
him you know. Good morning, Mr. Chambers, you know.
That's nice.
Yeah, Mr. Chambers, Money Johnson, and me. That was the quintet. Then later on I had an octet which was bongos and bongos and conga.
Was this still in the '40s or later?
Yeah, this was in the '40s, had Big Nick on tenor saxophone.
You know he's pretty active again. He lives in Richmond.
Yeah, I get Christmas cards from him. Big Nick on
He gets up to Washington pretty often.
Is that right? Big Nick on tenor saxophone, Joe Wilder on trumpet. Here's a picture of them. At last I've thought of that bass player's name with Cab. Al Morgan. (viz.- Cassette 4, p. 8)
That's right, now we solved that problem. But otherwise you just showed me a photo of the band you were just describing, Joe Wilder and Big Nick Nicholas and
My brother Jay on piano.
And Billy Taylor on bass.
Yeah, Billy Taylor, Jr. on bass.
And two percussions.
Mm hmm.
